ranking.reader: Artem, a full-stack engineer who builds web products and LLM agents and writes about both. He wants items he can learn from or act on as a builder, not general tech news.

topics.description: Agent and automated pipelines and harnesses, LLM assistants, self-hosted/private AI platform development, and LLM/inference optimization.
exclude: AI policy, lawsuits, regulation, company drama, funding and business news
coding agents and their add-ons (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, plugins, skills) used while writing code (they belong to Tooling)
consumer AI apps with no engineering substance
include: building, running or evaluating LLM systems: agent harnesses, tool use, MCP, RAG, evals
inference and serving: self-hosted/local models, quantization, speed and cost
major model, API or dev-platform releases that change what or how you build
topics.name: AI Engineering

topics.description: Tools developers use to build software: editors, CLIs, libraries, and AI coding tools.
exclude: components for building LLM systems: agent frameworks, inference servers, evals (they belong to AI Engineering)
games, consumer apps, and utilities with no role in software development
nostalgia or legacy-systems threads, career and workplace discussion
include: tools used while building software: editors and IDEs, CLIs, terminals, debuggers, build tools, package managers, version control, databases
AI tools used while writing code: coding agents, editor plugins, Claude Code skills and hooks
new or notably improved open-source libraries and frameworks for building software
topics.name: Tooling

topics.description: Product and web trends, securities & market data, data visualization, browser performance, web architecture, and SEO.
exclude: general tech-company news, earnings and stock moves with no product angle
AI model releases (AI Engineering) and developer tools (Tooling)
games and demos that merely run in a browser
include: the web platform and browsers: new APIs, standards, rendering and browser performance
frontend engineering and web architecture: frameworks, CSS, performance, SEO
data visualization, and products built on market or financial data
product and web trends: notable launches and how web products make money
topics.name: Web Products

items.summary: A Wall Street Journal election map combines county-level results and shifts into one visualization: spikes show victory margins and bend to show swing, styled like strands of hair.
items.title: Hairy election margins map

items.summary: A RAG question-answering system for real open-source issue trackers, evaluated on 95 hand-reviewed vitejs/vite questions with five configurations and scorer audits; retrieval improved weighted accuracy from 0.221 to 0.700 but raised fabrication from 1.1% to 20%.
items.title: zaxiu88888/issue-rag

items.summary: GPUWorks is a 40 MB GPU management and Model-as-a-Service platform that joins heterogeneous accelerators and public/private cloud instances into one cluster, deploying vLLM/SGLang models behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a 1,235-spec catalog.
items.title: Show HN: GPUWorks – A 40 MB GPU cluster manager for vLLM/SGLang, no K8s needed

items.summary: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is a generally available Gemini API/business video model adding native 15-second clips, multi-turn conversational editing, stronger reference adherence, and a 30% price cut to $0.07 per second for 720p.
items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash

items.summary: Ork is a source-available assistant for persistent bots that share conversations and work on isolated computers, with Tauri desktop and Expo mobile apps backed by an API and worker; the repository provides local Docker/PostgreSQL setup steps.
items.title: orkbot-run/ork

items.summary: Winc is a Rust-built desktop editor with its own rendering engine, claiming 119 ms cold start, 52 MB RAM with 100,000 lines open, and a 1 GB file editable/highlighted in 220 ms; it includes multi-cursor editing, diffs, Git, terminal, previews and signed updates.
items.title: DEEIX-AI/Winc

items.summary: Rune is a pre-release native GPU-rendered Rust UI framework for macOS, Windows, Linux and web with its own renderer, text, layout and springs; apps can run headless so agents can render PNGs, dump element trees and drive scripted input.
items.title: Rune: A native GPU-rendered Rust UI framework for macOS, Windows, Linux and web

items.summary: Firenook is a Rust implementation of Firebase emulators, shown with a terminal UI and demo; its Show HN title claims 40× faster writes and 10× less RAM, and the text shows Firestore, Auth, Storage, Functions and Pub/Sub starting in about 600–800 ms.
items.title: Show HN: Firenook – Firebase emulators in Rust: 40× faster writes, 10× less RAM

items.summary: A blog post on emulating boolean values in CSS using the true/false keywords, @property to register a custom property constrained to syntax "true | false" with an initial value and inherits: false, plus @container style() queries for conditional styling.
items.title: true or false in CSS

items.summary: A Smashing Magazine article on making immersive LLM chat experiences (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot and similar full-screen apps) accessible, framing accessibility as core to functional digital experiences and reframing chat UIs through WCAG and the social model of disability.
items.title: Making Immersive LLM Chat Experiences More Accessible

items.summary: A FlowingData post highlighting New York Times charts that track shifts in Texas counties over time, using a multi-line chart for each county, with all lines moving sharply left at the bottom.
items.title: Swings in Texas over the years

items.summary: Anthropic post laying out how it thinks about agent memory: knowledge Claude keeps between sessions as readable notes, plus "dreaming" — reflecting on logs in idle time, borrowed from sleep-time compute — with evaluations showing what each component contributes.
items.title: The Components of Agent Memory

items.summary: Ask HN thread asking readers to describe their current AI agentic setup: paid subscriptions and tiers, pay-as-you-go or local models, coding harnesses, orchestration/swarm tools and agent platforms, as a snapshot of how workflows changed over a year.
items.title: Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?

items.summary: GitHub repo for Poki, a macOS-only MCP server plus standalone terminal agent that plugs into Claude Code, Codex or other MCP clients so an agent can handle phone tasks; ships a native bridge and idevice tools, requires Xcode, Rust and Node 24.
items.title: JosssphZhou/poki

items.summary: GitHub repo for a Node/TypeScript MCP server bridging Roblox Studio and AI assistants (Claude, Cursor, Cline, ChatGPT), with tools to read the object tree, create and update Lua scripts, inspect properties and run playtests, plus a read-only mode.
items.title: HerdBuilderEstimate/roblox-studio-mcp

items.summary: Asm is a package registry and command-line tool for assembly projects; version 0.6.0 supports Linux x86-64, Linux ARM64, and Apple Silicon macOS 15+, with commands to create, build, test, inspect, and update projects.
items.title: stubbi/asm

items.summary: devvm is an isolated development sandbox that creates a VM with your project's detected toolchains and chosen coding agents; running devvm in a project folder opens a shell in that VM, and later runs reuse it.
items.title: devvmhq/devvm

items.summary: Spindle is a type-safe OCaml 5 web framework with its own RFC-strict HTTP/1.1 engine, Eio-native multicore handlers, type-derived JSON, generated OpenAPI docs, WebSockets, SSE, sessions, and SQLite/Postgres support.
items.title: Show HN: Spindle – a full-featured, type-safe web framework for OCaml 5

items.summary: New York Times visualization maps county-level shifts in 2026 midterm voting margins versus 2024 presidential margins using angled arrows, showing mostly blue Democratic shifts except a few small red ones in Maine and Minnesota.
items.title: Shift in margins for Midterms 2026, by county

items.summary: Washington Post live tracker by Dylan Moriarty shows the percentage of votes counted so far, with counting still underway.
items.title: Percentage of votes counted so far

items.summary: A FlowingData post noting that the New York Times' election Needle is live for the 2026 midterms, showing each party's chances of winning Senate and House control plus views for individual races.
items.title: Needle of uncertainty is live for Midterms 2026

items.summary: llama-modchip: ggml/llama.cpp kernel patches, quantization transcoders and runtime tools that run sparse MoE checkpoints entirely in system RAM with zero GPUs. It shrinks 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash to 56.56 GiB at 1.71 bpw so it fits 64 GB with a 256K KV cache, reporting up to ~44 tok/s prefill and 111 tok/s on 8-channel workstations.
items.title: Llama-modchip: 284B DeepSeek on 64GB RAM, no GPU

items.summary: An essay arguing agent memory needs an OpenTelemetry-style shared spec, touring today's incompatible formats (AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules, /memories, GitHub-side facts, memory MCP JSONL graphs) and existing proposals. Author builds LoreKit, which he says is one proposal among several, not a solution.
items.title: Agent memory needs its OpenTelemetry moment

items.summary: WebsiteBench: a benchmark where agents explore a live site in a browser and reverse-engineer a full-stack clone. 70 websites, 46,916 hidden test cases (302–2,016 each); a case passes only if functional checks pass and every visual checkpoint hits 0.99 SSIM. Runnable via pip package and harbor; code Apache-2.0.
items.title: TIGER-AI-Lab/WebsiteBench

items.summary: A reference explainer of the Model Context Protocol: hosts, servers and models, with servers advertising capabilities the app relays to the model. Notes MCP is JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout or one HTTP endpoint (not REST), plus methods, capability negotiation, transports and auth, with spec and tools links.
items.title: MCP Explained

items.summary: A Hacker News discussion of how Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" setting exposed passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files.
items.title: Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" exposes passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files

items.summary: GitHub blog post detailing its new Git storage architecture, which decouples storage from compute and only orders reference updates, letting it test 5,000 concurrent agents and 7,200 pushes per second to one repo with low-latency reads.
items.title: GitHub's new Git storage architecture

items.summary: Finallyshell: an open-source SSH client in Go that recreates FinalShell's layout with vertical, reorderable session tabs, libghostty-vt terminal engine, and passwords stored in the system keychain instead of a file.
items.title: TooonyChen/finallyshell

items.summary: A Nightingale article presents a classroom/workshop exercise on equitable data visualization, using Alexandra Bell’s “Counternarratives” to show how titles and editorial framing shape what readers take from charts; it starts with a non-chart warm-up.
items.title: Same Chart, Many Titles: A Classroom Exercise in Framing Data

items.summary: Text.js is a framework for building full-stack React apps that render inside console.log, with React 19, App Router routes/layouts, keyboard input, server rendering, and a custom reconciler/Yoga/RLE pipeline that emits only changed frames as console.log calls.
items.title: Text.js: Build full-stack React apps that render inside console.log
